_comment: THE cross-language color contract. Go, TypeScript and elisp each assert
their own table against this file, row for row, which is the only
mechanism that makes a divergence between the three fail loudly instead
of quietly.
It pins WHICH of the six colors a state or an error class takes, not
what that color's value is: each renderer keeps its own hex, because a
tab-bar background and a CSS dot legitimately want different shades of
the same idea. What may never differ is the ASSIGNMENT — a workspace
that reads green in one surface and red in another is the failure this
file exists to prevent.
'none' is a real answer, not a gap. The merge states deliberately carry
badges and glyphs instead of colors so they never spend one of the
six, and UNSPECIFIED is the absence of a verdict rather than a verdict
of its own.
TEAL IS THE SIXTH, and it exists because blue was carrying two
incompatible jobs. A single DORMANT state meant both 'we put this
session to sleep on purpose to reclaim ~500MB' and 'the backend
substrate is broken', so the most ordinary event in the system rendered
identically to a dead shim. HIBERNATED took the benign half, SEVERED
kept blue and the field number, and blue now means something is
actually wrong.
_precedence_comment: The six-color precedence, strongest claim first. Each color is a
strictly stronger claim about what the user CANNOT do than the one
beneath it, so the strongest true claim wins. This order is the SSM's
SQL prec ranks made readable; the SSM stays the sole precedence
authority and this must not reorder it.
TEAL SITS BETWEEN BLUE AND PURPLE — `hibernated` is rank 15 in the
SSM's prec table, directly below the blue band (severed 12, starting
14) and above purple's 20. That is deliberately NOT below green:
hibernation makes the SAME actionability claim blue does (you cannot
interact without paying a bring-up) and only its REASON is benign.
Ranking it below green would let a stale `thinking` row from the turn a
workspace was hibernated after mask a workspace that is genuinely
_error_classes_comment: A failure card takes the color of the state its class resolves the
workspace to — card color IS state color, from this one table, so a
user cannot see a purple workspace explained by a red card. INTERNAL
resolves BLUE and never teal: an error class is by definition evidence
that something broke, which is precisely what teal denies.
resolves blue (agent-repl's own machinery is compromised) and API
resolves purple (the vendor or the account has stopped the work).
